questions.question: With cacheComponents enabled, a component awaits an uncached database query and is NOT wrapped in Suspense or "use cache". What happens?
options: The whole route silently becomes dynamic, as in the previous model
The query result is cached forever by default
Next.js flags it during development and the prerender fails until you cache it or wrap it in Suspense
The component is skipped and renders nothing
questions.explanation: Cache Components requires every uncached or runtime access to be either cached with "use cache" or placed behind a Suspense boundary, so each route still produces a static shell.

questions.question: Why can't a "use cache" function call cookies() directly?
options: Cached output may be shared across users, so request-specific APIs are forbidden; read the cookie outside and pass the value as an argument
cookies() only works in Client Components
questions.explanation: Request-time APIs are not allowed inside cached scopes (even via helpers). Passing the extracted value as an argument makes it part of the cache key.

questions.question: A Server Action edits a fund's details and the editor must see the change on the very next render. Which call fits best?
questions.explanation: updateTag is Server-Action-only and expires the tag immediately, so the next request waits for fresh data (read-your-own-writes). revalidateTag with "max" serves stale data while refreshing.

questions.question: In a cacheLife profile, what does the `stale` value control?
options: How often the server regenerates the entry in the background
How long the browser's client router reuses the cached output without checking the server
When the entry is deleted with no traffic
How many instances share the entry
questions.explanation: stale is client-side; revalidate triggers a background refresh on the server; expire forces the next request to wait for fresh content after a period with no traffic.
